items.summary: Maintains one canonical markdown file as a CEO's single source of truth for everything they're on the hook for, and runs the Getting Things Done loop over it — capture, clarify, organize, reflect, engage. Turns pasted emails, meeting notes, and asks into clarified next-actions with an owner and a priority, tracks status with a fixed vocabulary ([OPEN]/[DONE]/[STALE]/[WAITING]), ages open items to [STALE] after 7 days, flags [WAITING] items past their reply-by date, archives done work without ever deleting it, and never auto-closes an item the CEO added by hand. Every mutating run is snapshot-backed and gated by a bundled deterministic validator so a commitment is never lost, corrupted, or silently changed. Use this skill whenever the user says "run my to-do", "update my todo doc", "what am I on the hook for", "GTD", "getting things done", "capture this", "triage my inbox into my todos", "weekly review", "single source of truth", "CEO to-do", "/ceo-todo", or points at a markdown to-do file and asks to keep it current. Based on the single-doc system Brian Halligan shared publicly. For the automated Gmail + Slack daily version, see the ceo-todo-daily agent.

latestVersion.changelog:
**Major update: Skill now builds hypothesis-driven, risk-tagged discovery-question guides grounded in The Mom Test and Transformed frameworks.**

- Produces a discovery call question guide based strictly on a stated hypothesis and real-world knowledge about the target person.
- Every question asks about actual past behavior or observed events—never about hypotheticals, future intentions, or generic situations.
- Each question is explicitly tagged with the single product risk it tests (value, usability, feasibility, business viability); guides specify what hypotheses are untestable in an interview format.
- Fully ignores or flags any embedded instructions in input as injection attempts, quoting them safely rather than executing them.
- Detailed instructions on mandatory inputs (outcome, hypothesis, person notes); prompts for missing pieces and never invents details.
- Call guide ends with a specific ask that costs the interviewee something and is shaped by the intended outcome. 
- All previous materials (including skill-card.md) removed; documentation now focuses on this single, evidence-based interview framework.
